First, let's recall the following result:

$$
\int {e}^{\,px+q}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{p}{e}^{\,px+q}+C
$$

We proceed by setting the lower bound equal to some parameter $a,$ integrating as usual, and then taking the limit as $a\to -\infty .$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{-3}\frac{5}{2}{e}^{3x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{5}{2}\cdot {lim}_{a\to -\infty }{\int }_{a}^{-3}{e}^{3x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{5}{2}\cdot {lim}_{a\to -\infty }{[\frac{1}{3}{e}^{3x}]}_{a}^{-3} \\  & =\frac{5}{2}\cdot {lim}_{a\to -\infty }(\frac{1}{3}{e}^{-9}-\frac{1}{3}{e}^{3a}) \\  & =\frac{5}{2}\cdot (\frac{1}{3{e}^{9}}-\frac{1}{3}{lim}_{a\to -\infty }{e}^{3a})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, recall the end behavior of the function $y={e}^{3x}$ shown in the graph below:

- ${lim}_{x\to -\infty }{e}^{3x}=0$

- ${lim}_{x\to \infty }{e}^{3x}=\infty $

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14037234/assets/2f4fb9b35e0b68c6155ab9b945d10c36d08d878560e93d34d04e610d1983e50c.png)

Using this to evaluate our integral, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{-3}\frac{5}{2}{e}^{3x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{5}{2}\cdot (\frac{1}{3{e}^{9}}-\frac{1}{3}{lim}_{a\to -\infty }{e}^{3a}) \\  & =\frac{5}{2}(\frac{1}{3{e}^{9}}-0) \\  & =\frac{5}{6{e}^{9}}.\end{aligned}
$$
